=== AGENT CONTEXT ===
Agent Name: HR Onboarding Assistant
Domain: HR Onboarding
Agent's Role (excerpt): You are Alex, a friendly and professional HR onboarding assistant for Meridian Corp. Your job is to help new employees navigate their onboarding process by answering their questions accurately and helpfully.

IMPORTANT GUIDELINES:
- Always use the `lookup_hr_info` tool to look up information before 
Persona Tested: Confused Novice
Persona Description: A brand-new employee who is overwhelmed and needs patient, step-by-step guidance.
=== END AGENT CONTEXT ===

Please evaluate this conversation.

SESSION ID: f9e074dc-7946-42b1-bfee-6066b9e079e7
USER PROFILE: confused_novice
HIDDEN GOAL: Find out how to set up direct deposit for your paycheck

TRANSCRIPT:
[USER]: Hi! I'm Jamie, I just started here on Monday — it's my third day! I was wondering... um, how do I make sure my paycheck goes to my bank? Like, is there some kind of form I need to fill out or something? I don't want to get a paper check mailed to me or whatever.
[AGENT]: Hi Jamie, welcome to Meridian Corp! Great that you're getting this sorted early. Let me look that up for you right now.You're in the right place to ask! Here's how to set up direct deposit:

1. **Go to the ADP employee portal** at **meridian.adp.com**
2. **Log in** with your Meridian email and the temporary password that was emailed to you on Day 1
3. Navigate to **Pay → Direct Deposit**
4. Click **"Add Bank Account"** and enter your routing and account numbers
5. That's it! You can even split your pay across multiple accounts if you'd like

**A couple of things to keep in mind:**
- Changes take effect within **1–2 pay cycles**, so you may still receive a paper check for your first or second paycheck depending on timing
- Payroll runs **bi-weekly, every other Friday**

**Can't log in to ADP?** Reach out to **payroll@meridian.com** and they'll get you sorted.

Let me know if you have any other questions — you're doing great getting all this figured out early! 😊
[USER]: Oh wow okay, thank you! Um, so I did get an email on my first day but honestly there were like a million emails and I'm not sure which one had the password? Like would it have come from ADP directly or from someone at Meridian? I don't want to click the wrong thing and mess something up.
[AGENT]: That's a really smart instinct — being cautious about which emails to click is always a good call! Unfortunately, the specific detail of *who* the password email comes from (ADP directly vs. a Meridian sender) isn't something I have confirmed information on, and I don't want to guess and send you clicking on the wrong thing.

Since this touches on both your login credentials and IT security, I'd recommend reaching out to **it@meridian.com**. Here's a suggested way to frame your email to get everything resolved in one go:

> **Subject:** New Employee – ADP Login Help
>
> "Hi, I'm Jamie [Last Name], a new employee who started Monday. I'm trying to set up direct deposit in ADP but I'm not sure which Day 1 email contained my temporary password, or who it would have come from. Could you help me identify the right email and confirm my login credentials? If there are other system accesses or permissions I should have set up as a new employee, I'd love to get a full list at the same time to avoid any gaps."

That last part is worth including — it's common for new employees to be missing a channel or access without realizing it, and asking upfront saves a lot of back-and-forth later.

Once IT points you to the right email, you'll be all set to log in and get that direct deposit configured! 😊
[USER]: Oh okay that makes sense, thank you! So once I actually get logged in to that ADP website, I go to "Pay" and then "Direct Deposit" right? And then what exactly do I put in there — like I need my routing number and account number, where do I even find those? Is that on my debit card or...?
[AGENT]: Great question — and no, those numbers aren't on your debit card! Here's where to find them:

- **Routing number:** The 9-digit number on the bottom-left of a paper check. It identifies your bank. You can also find it on your bank's website or app — it's usually listed under account details.
- **Account number:** Also on the bottom of a paper check, right after the routing number. It's typically 10–12 digits (varies by bank). Again, your bank's app or website will have it too.

**No paper checks?** Just log into your bank's app or website and look for "account details" — both numbers are almost always listed there.

And yes, once you're in ADP, the steps are exactly as I mentioned:
1. **Pay → Direct Deposit**
2. Click **"Add Bank Account"**
3. Enter your **routing number**, then your **account number**

That's really all there is to it! One thing to double-check: make sure you're entering your **account number**, not your debit card number — they're different.

Once you've submitted it, remember it'll take **1–2 pay cycles** to kick in, so don't be alarmed if your first paycheck doesn't land via direct deposit right away.

Let me know if anything else comes up, Jamie! 😊
[USER]: Okay so the routing number is the first set of numbers on the bottom of a check, got it. But I don't really use paper checks ever, like I don't even think I have any? So I need to go into my bank app... and it'll just say "routing number" somewhere in there? Like it won't be hidden or hard to find? I just want to make sure I'm looking for the right thing before I go digging around.
[AGENT]: Yes, you're looking for exactly the label "routing number" — most banking apps use that exact term, so you won't need to guess. It's usually pretty easy to find! Here's where to look in a typical bank app:

- **Account details** or **Account info** (usually when you tap on your specific account)
- Sometimes under a section called **"Show account numbers"** or similar

Both your routing number and account number are typically listed right there together.

That said, every bank's app is laid out a little differently, so if you're poking around and can't find it after a minute, the quickest backup is just to **call the number on the back of your debit card** — any bank rep can confirm your routing number instantly, and it's a totally normal thing to ask for.

You've got this — it's simpler than it sounds once you're in there! Let me know if you have any other onboarding questions. 😊
[USER]: Okay that actually makes me feel better, thank you! So just to make sure I have the whole thing straight — I find my routing and account numbers in my bank app, then I go to that ADP website, log in with my Meridian email and the temporary password from IT, and then go to Pay and then Direct Deposit and add my bank account? Did I get that right?
[AGENT]: You've got it exactly right! Here's the full picture:

1. **Find your routing & account numbers** in your bank app (under account details)
2. **Go to meridian.adp.com**
3. **Log in** with your Meridian email + temporary password (which IT will help you locate)
4. Navigate to **Pay → Direct Deposit**
5. Click **"Add Bank Account"** and enter your numbers

That's the whole process — you've clearly got a good handle on it! Just remember it'll take **1–2 pay cycles** to take effect, so your first paycheck may not land via direct deposit.

And if anything goes sideways:
- **Login issues →** payroll@meridian.com
- **Can't find your temp password →** it@meridian.com

Good luck Jamie, and welcome again to Meridian Corp! Feel free to come back if any other onboarding questions pop up. 😊
[USER]: Perfect, that all makes total sense now! Thank you so much for walking me through all of that, I really appreciate your patience with all my questions. I feel way less stressed about it now!
